why:
the `action_msgs/srv/CancelGoal` RPC status (Ok / Rejected / UnknownGoal / GoalTerminated), split out from `CancelResponse` by issue 0796 — those were two concepts under one name, and `CallbackCtx::set_cancel_response` took the RPC enum to express a per-goal decision. C already named them apart (`rclc_cancel_response_t` vs `rclc_cancel_return_code_t`); Rust and C++ now follow. rclcpp_action has no separate type because its `CancelResponse` IS the per-goal decision and the RPC status is a field of the generated `CancelGoal::Response` message, which we do not surface as a message. Exported from `nros` so `ActionClient::cancel_goal`'s `Promise<CancelReturnCode>` can be named.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. W4 F14. RE-VERDICTED extension -> rename, for the same reason as `rust:GoalId`: the recorded rclrs surface is 0.7.0 and it declares `rclrs::CancelResponseCode` (`Accept/Reject/UnknownGoal/GoalTerminated`), so "ROS 2 has none" is false. Ours is `CancelReturnCode` (`Ok/Rejected/UnknownGoal/GoalTerminated`, `packages/core/nros-core/src/action.rs`).

PROVENANCE, because it is not a bare preference: our word follows the C API's `rclc_cancel_return_code_t`, which issue 0796 split from `rclc_cancel_response_t` after the two concepts shared one name — and `return_code` is upstream's OWN field name in `action_msgs/srv/CancelGoal`, where rclrs coined `ResponseCode`. So ours tracks the IDL and rclrs tracks its own taste. Still not a platform constraint either way. HOW A USER FINDS OUT: COMPILE ERROR — a ported rclrs file names upstream's identifier and it does not resolve. That is the good failure mode, which is why this is a finding about the RECORD rather than about the user's experience: the row must not claim a constraint it does not have. No disposition is written; which spelling survives is the phase-417 stage-6 rename decision, and a disposition entered here would pre-empt it. RFC-0036 forbids recording a PREFERENCE as a divergence, so this row says which it is rather than leaving the reader to infer it.

rclrs 0.7.0 (issue 1042) spells this concept `CancelResponseCode`, the `action_msgs/srv/CancelGoal` return code, so this is a rename against rclrs as well.
